frequency_question: How often do expiring major water treaties secure a signed successor agreement before or near their expiration date, given visible initial signals?
membership_rule: Includes formal treaties governing shared river basins between sovereign states that reached expiration dates and required formal renewal or replacement. Excludes unratified drafts and non-binding joint declarations without water allocation provisions.

cases.name: Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase agreements

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named historical benchmarks; captures major bilateral framework renewals.
known_gaps: Excludes minor tributary adjustments or purely domestic water management pacts.
skeleton: 5 documented major renewal/successor negotiations for permanent or long-term transboundary river treaties globally within comparable interstate friction environments.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 comparable major historical renewal instances where advance signals of negotiation were present.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy norms change slowly over decades, keeping this base rate stable through the end of the decade.
